title: AI-generated women spread disinformation about Singapore on TikTok
summary: CNA reports that AI-generated female personas are spreading disinformation about Singapore on TikTok.
attribution: Unknown; the headline does not name an operator.
motive: Unknown; the headline says only that the accounts spread disinformation about Singapore.
vector: AI-generated female personas posting on TikTok.
impact: Disinformation about Singapore is reaching TikTok audiences; the scale is not stated.

timeline.event: Reported by channelnewsasia.com via Hacker News

title: Deepfakes tear apart a high school community, per 404 Media
summary: 404 Media reports that deepfakes disrupted and divided a high school. Location, perpetrators and details are not given in the headline.
vector: Deepfake media targeting people at a high school.
impact: A high school community was seriously disrupted; the number of victims is not stated.

title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Rep. Van Orden over AI deepfake videos
summary: Attorneys for Democratic candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to Rep. Derrick Van Orden over his use of deepfake videos ahead of the November election.
attribution: Alleged by the Cooke campaign's attorneys in a cease-and-desist letter; not independently confirmed in the summary.
motive: Political advantage in the November congressional race (alleged).
vector: Deepfake videos of the opposing candidate.
impact: Deepfake videos depicting a congressional candidate circulated during an election campaign.
response: Cooke campaign attorneys sent a cease-and-desist letter to Van Orden.

title: AI-built typosquat sites deliver SmartRAT via ClickFix
summary: Zscaler ThreatLabz observed typosquatting domains in March 2026 hosting lure content made with AI website-creation tools, running a ClickFix campaign that delivers SmartRAT.
attribution: Not stated in the summary; described only as threat actors using AI website builders.
vector: Typosquatted domains with AI-generated lure pages using ClickFix to deliver the SmartRAT malware.
root_cause: AI website builders let attackers quickly create convincing lures at scale.
impact: Unknown; the summary gives no victim counts or losses.
response: Zscaler ThreatLabz observed and analysed the campaign.

title: Langflow code injection RCE (CVE-2026-9198) added to CISA KEV as actively exploited
target: Langflow AI workflow platform default deployments
summary: CISA lists a Langflow code injection flaw that lets unauthenticated attackers get full remote code execution on default deployments as actively exploited.
attribution: Not stated in the CISA KEV entry.
vector: Unauthenticated code injection against default Langflow deployments, giving remote code execution.
root_cause: Code injection vulnerability in Langflow that can be reached without authentication on default configurations.
impact: Full remote code execution on exposed default Langflow instances. Number of victims is not stated.
response: CISA added CVE-2026-9198 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

title: prt-scan: AI-powered campaign exploits pull_request_target via six accounts
summary: Wiz traced the prt-scan supply chain campaign, an AI-powered effort exploiting pull_request_target, to a single actor using six accounts, active about three weeks before it was noticed.
attribution: Wiz Research linked six accounts to one actor and traced activity to three weeks before detection; no named group.
vector: AI-powered abuse of GitHub pull_request_target workflows through six attacker accounts.
root_cause: Exploitable pull_request_target workflow configurations in targeted repositories.
impact: Unknown; the summary gives no victim count or loss figures.
response: Wiz published its analysis of the campaign; no other response is stated.

title: TeamPCP trojanizes LiteLLM versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 to steal credentials
summary: Malicious LiteLLM versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 abuse Python's .pth mechanism for stealthy persistence and exfiltrate cloud credentials, CI/CD secrets and keys to attacker-controlled domains.
attribution: Wiz Research describes it as a continuation of TeamPCP's open-source attack spree, with LiteLLM the latest victim.
motive: Credential and secret theft (cloud credentials, CI/CD secrets, keys).
vector: Trojanized LiteLLM releases (1.82.7, 1.82.8) using Python .pth files for persistence and exfiltration.
root_cause: Unknown; the summary does not say how the malicious versions were published.
impact: Malware exfiltrates cloud credentials, CI/CD secrets and keys to attacker-controlled domains. Number of victims is not stated.
response: Wiz Research published an analysis of the malicious versions; other response actions are not stated.
